issue.title: Upload file names with Cyrillic letters come back garbled
issue.body:
We name statement files after the bank and the account, partly in Russian. The
import works, but `GET /uploads/:id` returns the name garbled: a file uploaded
as `банк_вклад.csv` comes back as `Ð±Ð°Ð½Ðº_Ð²ÐºÐ»Ð°Ð´.csv`. It isn't only
Cyrillic: `relevé_octobre.csv` from our Lyon office comes back as
`relevÃ©_octobre.csv`. Our reconciliation script matches uploads to files by
name, so it can't find these. Names in plain ASCII are fine.
## Discussion

### ben-ops (maintainer) · 2026-11-09
Thanks. Are these uploaded through the web form, or by your own script?

### riga-shared-services · 2026-11-09
Both. The web form in Chrome and our curl script give the same result.

input.title: Decode non-ASCII upload file names as UTF-8
input.body:
File: src/api/uploads.ts

multer (busboy) hands back file.originalname decoded as latin1, so UTF-8 bytes of names like `банк_вклад.csv` or `relevé_octobre.csv` become mojibake. The POST handler stores file.originalname as `filename` (and in the storage key). Re-decode it once, e.g. `Buffer.from(file.originalname, "latin1").toString("utf8")`, and use that value for the extension check, uploadKey and createUploadWithJob, so GET /uploads/:id returns the original name. ASCII names are unchanged. Add a test with a Cyrillic and an accented name.

file: src/api/uploads.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The upload handler stores `file.originalname` as-is. multer decodes multipart file names as latin1, so UTF-8 names are garbled when they are saved. That matches both the Cyrillic and the `é` examples, and it explains why the web form and curl give the same result. `GET /uploads/:id` only returns the stored name. The draft PR (pr-10) re-decodes the name as UTF-8 on upload. Names already stored will stay garbled unless they are re-decoded.
